transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I came in because this has been going on a long time. I’m still doing my routes and my volunteer shifts, but most days there’s this heavy, low feeling on me. It’s like I’m just going through the motions instead of really being part of my own life.
Did this low feeling start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
Yeah… I’d say it started after my father died. That was about three years ago, and I’ve kind of had this low feeling hanging around since then.
Do you find that this low feeling is mainly about missing your father and his death?
I’m not really sure. I do miss him, yeah, but it doesn’t always feel like it’s only about that. It’s more like the low feeling just stuck around, if that makes sense.
For the past two years, have you felt down or low more days than not?

Yes. Most days for a long time now, I’ve had this heavy, low feeling on me. I still get through my routes and my volunteer shifts, but a lot of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yeah… I guess I do feel that way sometimes. It’s not like I’m thinking everything is over, but most days there’s this heavy low feeling, like I’m just getting through my routes and volunteer shifts without really feeling like I’m in my own life.
In the past two years, has there ever been a stretch of more than two months when you did not feel down most days?
No, I don’t think so. It’s been pretty steady for about three years now, since my father died. I might have better days here and there, but not a couple months where it really lifted.
During these past three years, was there ever a period when your depression became much worse than usual for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. It’s been pretty steady, like low most of the time. I can’t think of a clear two-week stretch where it got a lot worse than the usual.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. I still do the things I usually do, but… I don’t really know if I enjoy them the same way. It’s hard to tell sometimes.
Do you often think poorly of yourself?

Yeah… I do. I compare myself a lot to the kind of man my dad was, and I feel like I don’t measure up. Nobody’s really saying I’m failing, but in my own head I keep thinking I should be further along, handling things better than I am.
Do you often feel low on energy or easily fatigued?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially after work, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s more than normal.
Have you often had trouble sleeping?

Yeah, sometimes. Especially the night before I’ve got a run, I’ll lie there thinking about the next day’s stops. Or I’ll wake up around four and then I don’t really get back to sleep. I still get to work on time, but I feel like I’m starting the day already worn down.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?
I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly. I do get keyed up about things sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of myself as being on edge all the time.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying?
I’m not sure I’d say a lot. I think about bills and work and normal stuff, but I haven’t really kept track of it as worrying all the time.
When you feel low, is it usually triggered by thoughts about your father or his death?

Not really just about my father, no. It’s more like… for a long time I’ve had this heavy, low feeling most days. I still get through my routes and my volunteer shifts, but a lot of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions, not really in my own life.
Would you say anxiety is a major part of what’s been bothering you?
No, I don’t think anxiety is the main thing. I get worried here and there like anybody, but what’s been bothering me feels more like being worn down than being anxious.
Have you often had a poor appetite or overeaten?
I haven’t really noticed a big change there. My appetite seems pretty normal most of the time, and I don’t think I’ve been overeating much.
Do you often have trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Yeah, some. I can still do my job, but I notice it more lately. I’ll be looking at delivery times and have to reread them, or I’ll stand there staring at the schedule board longer than I should. It’s like my mind just doesn’t lock onto things the way it used to.
During this time, have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly all day, every day?

Yeah… I’d say yes. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything, but for a long time now there’s been this heavy, low feeling most days. I still get through my routes and my volunteer shifts, but a lot of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions instead of really being in my own life.
During the times your depression felt at its worst, did you have thoughts that life wasn’t worth living?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had clear thoughts like that… it’s more just feeling worn down and low. But I can’t say I’ve been thinking life isn’t worth living.
At any time during these past three years, did you have a two-week period when you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?

I’m not sure I’d say almost everything. I’ve had stretches where I didn’t feel like doing much and things felt kind of flat, but I don’t know that there was a full two weeks where I lost interest in nearly everything.
